title: Why You Hear Your Name When No One Called It
hook: Your brain can trick you into hearing voices.

narration.text: Ever swear you heard your name, but no one was there?
This is your brain's 'top-down processing' at work.
It uses expectations and past experiences to interpret incomplete sounds.
Your brain is constantly predicting what it expects to hear next.
When ambient noise is ambiguous, your brain fills in the gaps.
It prioritises familiar, meaningful sounds, like your own name.
This makes you perceive a distinct call, even if it was just background noise.
It is a normal, everyday auditory illusion.
Has this ever happened to you?

description: Discover the fascinating reason your brain sometimes makes you hear your name, even when no one is speaking. It is all about how your brain interprets sounds, a process called top-down processing.
topic: Why you sometimes think you heard your name called when no one spoke, explaining the brain's top down processing of sound.
